newsitem.title: UK: Top executives helping Britain's Blair - paper.
newsitem.headline: Top executives helping Britain's Blair - paper.

text.p: Senior executives from companies ranging from British Airways to media and leisure group Pearson Plc are advising opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair on his economic and industrial policies, the Observer reported on Sunday.

It said British Airways chief executive Robert Ayling, Pearson's chairman-designate Dennis Stevenson, Unilever chairman Niall Fitzgerald and others had been briefing Blair at a series of weekly private dinners.
It quoted Labour sources as saying the executives were acting privately and were not necessarily endorsing the party in the next national election, which must be called by May 22.

The newspaper also said George Simpson, managing director of defence and industrial giant General Electric Co Plc, and British Aerospace chairman Bob Bauman were preparing to sign a manifesto that would back centre-left business policies such as a minimum wage and the European Union's controversial Social Chapter, opposed by ruling Conservatives.
The report would be published on Tuesday at a conference addressed by Blair and Simpson, it said.
